title: What is known about 1RB0LD_1LC0RD_1LA0LC_1RE0LB_1RB1RF_0LD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_1LC0RD_1LA0LC_1RE0LB_1RB1RF_0LD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open; one rule is known. At the moments when the head is in state B at the left end the tape starts B> 000 (100)^a (010)^b 01, followed by more blocks. Then (100)a (010)b+2a+1 goes to (100)4a (010)b: a counter that quadruples while the 010s pay for it (10 → 40 → 160 in the run). When they run out, the remainder and the blocks further right decide among many different shapes (blocks of 001, 1001, 0100100), which are not yet mapped.

Third pass (12 November). Seen from the left end, the tape is a list of runs of 100 and the machine is a list rewriting system with thirteen exact rules (quadrupling, flips by parity, carries, restarts), which predict all 46 events of the run from blank tape up to step 1.95·1011. One way to halt is known exactly: a quadrupling round that uses up the second run to the last copy while more runs follow. That needs an exact hit, with chance about (log b)/b per phase, so the machine probably never halts; no halt occurs in 1018 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 56,320 cells have been visited and 26,496 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.509). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.059).

claims.title: The run from blank tape
claims.text: B-at-the-left-end events include (100)<sup>10</sup> (010)<sup>250</sup> → (100)<sup>40</sup> (010)<sup>229</sup> → (100)<sup>160</sup> (010)<sup>148</sup>, then (100)<sup>171</sup> 1 (100)<sup>298</sup> 1, …, (100)<sup>5647</sup> (010)<sup>2686</sup> 01 at step 255,057,568.

claims.title: Same transition table as 1RB0LC_1RC1RF_1LD0RA_1LE0LD_1RC0LA_0LA---
claims.text: Renaming the states A→E, B→C, C→D, D→A, E→B, F→F turns this table into the one of 1RB0LC_1RC1RF_1LD0RA_1LE0LD_1RC0LA_0LA--- (found by comparing all 720 renamings with every holdout); only the start state differs, so the two runs from blank tape are different runs of one machine and every rule found for one holds for the other.
claims.where: the two tables, state by state

claims.title: The quadrupling round, exact
claims.text: B> 000 (100)^c (010)^(b+2c+1) X → B> 000 (100)^(4c) (010)^b X in 60c²+13c+39 steps (c ≥ 3), for any tape X to the right: checked by direct simulation for c = 3..39, b = 0..7 and four tails X (1,184 cases, step counts included); the round never looks at X.

claims.title: The tape is a list of runs of 100, with exact rules
claims.text: Sampled when the head is at the left end in state B reading 000, the tape is 000 (100)^n1 s1 (100)^n2 s2 … (100)^nk 1 with separators 0, 1 or 00, written [n1 s1, …, nk 1]. The first run quadruples, paid 2c+1 at a time by the second ([c 0, b s, …] → [4c 0, b−2c−1 s, …]); when the second run cannot pay, a flip rewrites the front ([c 0, b 1] → [2c−b−1 1, 2b+2 1] for b even, [2 0, 2c−b−3 0, 2b+2 1] for b odd; [c 1, d 1] → [2c−d−1 0, 2d+2 1] or [2c−d+1 0, 2d+1 1]; carries into a third and fourth run), and [2 0, x …] restarts the counter at 10. Thirteen rules, each checked against direct simulation for every parameter below 40: 60,000 cases, all agree. Lists with odd runs below the front follow rules not yet written.

claims.title: The run from blank tape follows the rules to step 1.95·10<sup>11</sup>
claims.text: The first 46 events of the run from blank tape (direct simulation), from [2 0, 2 1] at step 91 to [163840 0, 27983 1] at step 195,343,860,508, are each the one the rules predict. The two start states of this table (the two holdouts) give the same events at the same steps.

claims.title: One exact way to halt
claims.text: [c 0, 2c+1 1, d s, …] → [4c 01, d s, …] → halt before the next event, for c ≥ 3: a quadrupling round that uses up the second run exactly, in a list of at least three runs with second separator 1. Checked for c = 3..39 with many tails (3,498 cases); [640 0, 98 01, 162 1] halts after 5,029,947 steps. With two runs only, [4c 01] does not halt.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>18</sup> steps
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 6 cells, whole runs of equal blocks crossed at once, exact step counts) runs 10<sup>18</sup> steps from blank tape without a halt.
claims.where: holdouts/1RB0LE_0RC1RC_0RD1LA_1LD0LA_1LF1LC_---0LA/py/check_msim.py run 1RB0LD_1LC0RD_1LA0LC_1RE0LB_1RB1RF_0LD--- 1e18 (macro simulator c/msim.c there, checked against the direct simulator at 109 steps by check_msim.py check)

claims.title: No pushdown certificate with a DFA of at most 6 states
claims.text: The pushdown reduction of bb6-1RB0LF_1RC0LB/c/pds.c (one side of the tape kept exactly, the other abstracted by a DFA, reachability by post* saturation) reaches a halt for every DFA with at most 6 states, on either side (run for 1RB0LC_1RC1RF_1LD0RA_1LE0LD_1RC0LA_0LA---; the twin has the same table).

claims.title: Probably non-halting
claims.text: The known halt needs the second run to be hit exactly: b = (2c+1) + (8c+1) + … for the counter c at which a phase starts (10 or 8 after a restart). For a second run of size b that is about log<sub>4</sub> b targets among b values, a chance of about (log b)/b per phase, and b roughly doubles from flip to flip (it is above 10<sup>5</sup> now). The sum converges and is small. This assumes the remainders behave like random numbers and that no other list shape halts; neither is proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. One exact way to halt is known (a quadrupling round that uses up the second run exactly, in a list of three or more runs); the run from blank tape has not met it in 10<sup>18</sup> steps and the chance that it ever does looks small, but nothing is proved. The rules for lists with odd runs below the front are not written, so other ways to halt are not excluded.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LC_1RC1RF_1LD0RA_1LE0LD_1RC0LA_0LA--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows, but probably not. Seen from the left end, the tape is a list of runs of 100; the first run quadruples and the second pays for it. The machine stops only if the second run is used up to the last copy at the wrong moment, an exact hit that has not happened in 1018 steps.

facts.text: No halt in the macro simulator.
The list rules; they predict all 46 events from blank tape to step 1.95·10<sup>11</sup>.
Halting needs the second run to equal one of about log b values; chance about (log b)/b per phase.

sections.heading: A counter that quadruples
html: When the head is in state B at the left end, the tape starts with a block of a copies of 100 and then b copies of 010. One pass turns this into 4a copies of 100 and b − 2a − 1 copies of 010: the counter quadruples, and the 010s pay. In the run: 10 → 40 → 160 while b goes 250 → 229 → 148.
When the 010s cannot pay any more, the leftover and the blocks to the right decide what comes next, and that produces many different shapes; this part is not yet understood.

sections.heading: A counter that quadruples
html: Look at the tape whenever the head is back at the left end in state B reading 000. It then reads 000 (100)^c (010)^b …: a counter of c copies of 100, a block of b copies of 010, then the rest of the tape. Each pass multiplies the counter by four and pays for it with 2c+1 copies of 010:
whatever lies further right. In the run the counter starts at 10 and goes 10, 40, 160, 640, … until the block cannot pay; what happens then depends on what is left and starts the next stage.
This table is the same as the one of 1RB0LC_1RC1RF_1LD0RA_1LE0LD_1RC0LA_0LA--- with the states renamed; the two holdouts differ only in the state they start in.

sections.heading: A list of runs, and one way to stop
html: Write [n1 s1, n2 s2, …] for the tape 000 (100)^n1 s1 (100)^n2 s2 …. The machine only ever works on the front of this list. While the second run can pay, the first quadruples: [c 0, b …] → [4c 0, b−2c−1 …]. When it cannot, a flip rewrites the two runs, for example [c 0, b 1] → [2c−b−1 1, 2b+2 1] when b is even, and the parity of b decides whether a new small head [2 0 …] is pushed in front, which restarts the counter at 10. Odd remainders carry the flip deeper into the list.

The machine halts when a quadrupling round leaves exactly zero copies of the second run while further runs follow: [c 0, 2c+1 1, d …] → [4c 01, d …] → halt. For a second run of a hundred thousand copies only a handful of values do this, and the run doubles at each flip, so the chances shrink quickly. That is why the machine probably runs forever, and also why this is hard to prove: one has to show the exact hit never happens.

sections.heading: What is left
html: Write the flip for every parity pattern of the list (the thirteen rules cover the cases met so far, not lists with odd runs further down), so that the list map can be iterated with big integers; make the halting chance precise; and prove the quadrupling round in Lean for all c.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.509). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.059).
After 109 steps the tape spans 56,320 cells (39,454 left of the start, 83 right), with a density of 1s of 0.47.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

family: List of runs of 100: a quadrupling counter paid by the second run, flips and carries; halts on an exact hit (same table as 1RB0LC_1RC1RF_1LD0RA_1LE0LD_1RC0LA_0LA---, other start state)
summary: One table, two start states (with 1RB0LC_1RC1RF_1LD0RA_1LE0LD_1RC0LA_0LA---). Tape = list [n1 s1, ..., nk 1] of runs of 100; the first run quadruples, paid 2c+1 at a time by the second; flips/carries/restarts by parity (13 rules, 60,000 cases checked; 46 events from blank to step 1.95e11 all predicted). Halts iff (known way) [c 0, 2c+1 1, d ...] is met: an exact hit, chance ~log(b)/b per phase; probably non-halting. No halt in 1e18 steps (macro simulator). No pushdown certificate with a DFA of <= 6 states.
